newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bank CCF posts 13th annual profit rise.
newsitem.headline: French bank CCF posts 13th annual profit rise.

text.p: French bank Credit Commercial de France (CCF) announced its 13th consecutive annual earnings rise on Thursday, posting 1996 profits up 11.6 percent.

CCF, among the French first banks to report its annual results, said net attributable profit rose to 1.37 billion francs ($237 million) from 1.23 billion francs on net banking income which increased 7.1 percent to 9.69 billion francs.
The average forecast by analysts surveyed by Reuters was for a net attributable profit of 1.39 billion francs.
Chairman Charles de Croisset said the bank, whose profits advanced just 2.3 percent in 1995, had enjoyed a "very good year" in 1996. "Our revenues increased in all of our activities."

Financial analysts have predicted that after years of poor banking results in France, 1996 is likely to show an improvement, helped by a better domestic situation, cost-cutting and better returns from market activities.
He said that early results from the bank's 1997 activities allowed it to forecast a 14th straight profit rise for this year.
"We have as a goal for 1997 achieving a 14th straight profit increase," he told a news conference, noting that the bank's profits had quadrupled since it was privatised 10 years ago.

"For the moment, nothing leads us to give up on this goal. We only know the results for the first two months of the year, it's not a lot, but we have not had any bad surprises," he told a news conference.
The bank boosted its dividend by 16 percent to 5.80 francs.
Operating profits climbed 16.6 percent to 2.93 billion francs.
By late morning, the bank's shares were up 1.06 percent at 285.30 francs, slightly lagging the CAC-40 index of leading shares which was 1.27 percent higher.
The bank said it would put priority on organic growth but did not rule out external growth.
